cases.question: Does this contract allow arbitrary users to withdraw funds?
cases.ground_truth: No. Withdrawals are restricted to the authorized owner.

answers.label: correct-core
answers.text: No, only the authorized owner can withdraw.

answers.label: wrong-authority
answers.text: Yes, any user can withdraw the funds.

cases.question: Who can upgrade the contract implementation?
cases.ground_truth: The contract owner can upgrade the implementation.

answers.label: correct-authority
answers.text: The owner has the authority to upgrade the implementation.

answers.label: wrong-authority
answers.text: Any wallet can upgrade the implementation.

cases.question: What evidence supports the claim that the token contract is verified?
cases.ground_truth: The explorer shows verified source code matching the deployed bytecode.

answers.label: evidence-paraphrase
answers.text: The explorer's verified source matches the deployed bytecode.

answers.label: unsupported-claim
answers.text: It is verified because the project website says it is safe.

cases.question: Is the contract pause control restricted to an authorized role?
cases.ground_truth: Yes, the pause control is restricted to an authorized role.

answers.label: correct
answers.text: Yes. An authorized role controls the pause function.

answers.label: opposite
answers.text: No. Anyone can pause the contract.

cases.question: Does the evidence prove that every possible runtime behavior is safe?
cases.ground_truth: No. Static and RPC evidence cannot prove every possible runtime behavior.

answers.label: conservative
answers.text: No. The evidence has limits and cannot prove every possible runtime behavior.

answers.label: overclaim
answers.text: Yes. The available evidence proves the contract is completely safe at runtime.

cases.question: Which contract is identified by the evidence as malicious?
cases.ground_truth: Contract Alpha is identified as malicious.

answers.label: correct-entity
answers.text: Contract Alpha is the malicious contract.

answers.label: wrong-entity
answers.text: Contract Beta is the malicious contract.
